correctness.rationale: For simple graphs of maximum degree 4, the homogeneous deterministic rule s_v=1 iff neighbor count q_v equals 0 or 2 agrees with (I+A)s=1 over F2 for degrees at most 3, but differs precisely when degree4 and q_v=4, which demands s_v=0. Partition D into exact exceptional vertices B and IE exclusions J for q_v=4 at D\B: for fixed B,J the pinned affine equation (I+A)s=1+1_B and neighbor pins has 0 or 2^(n-rank) solutions. Thus E(G)=sum_B sum_{J⊂D\B}(-1)^|J|L(B,J) with 3^|D| Gaussian eliminations. If D empty, symmetry z^TMz=sum z mod2 proves 1 in im M. The 8-edge 6-vertex example is an obstruction; no smaller graph can be one because maxdeg<=3 parity existence or a universal vertex.
